rows.head: Suzuki sparks a Canadiens comeback
rows.story: Nick Suzuki was back in the lineup after missing six games. It was a busy first period. Logan Cooley opened the scoring for the Mammoth less than two minutes in, and he scored again on the power play midway through the period to make it 2-0.

rows.head: Four points for McDavid, but the Oilers lose
rows.story: Pavel Mintyukov had a Gordie Howe hat trick: a goal, an assist and a fight. Mintyukov, who scores in about 1 game in 13, scored twice. Cutter Gauthier got the scoring started for the Ducks on the power play midway through the first, his fourth straight game with a goal.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

chips: First goal for a new club
rows.head: The Hurricanes edge the Islanders
rows.story: Logan Stankoven and Jesperi Kotkaniemi scored less than three minutes apart early in the first to put the Hurricanes up 2-0. It was a busy second period. Mitchell Chaffee scored his first goal for the Islanders early in the period to get the Islanders on the board.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Stamkos wins it in overtime
rows.story: Ross Colton got the scoring started for the Predators early in the first, but Jaden Schwartz tied it up for Colorado midway through the period. Vitali Pinchuk, undrafted and in his seventh NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Reid Schaefer, later in the period to put the Preds back ahead 2-1. Parker Kelly tied it 2-2 for Colorado early in the second.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

rows.head: The Devils blow a three-goal lead, then win it in overtime
rows.story: Luke Hughes struck first for the Devils early in the first. The second period was a wild one. Jake Neighbours and Timo Meier fought early in the period, and Anthony Mantha made it 2-0 for the Devils midway through the period.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

chips: First goal for a new club
rows.head: The Rangers squeak past the Flyers
rows.story: Gabe Perreault got the scoring started for the Rangers early in the first, but Simon Benoit scored his first goal for Philadelphia midway through the second to tie it 1-1. Noel Acciari put the Flyers up 2-1 just under two minutes later, and that was all they would get. Pavel Dorofeyev and Tye Kartye scored a minute and a half apart with just over six minutes left to turn a 2-1 deficit into a 3-2 lead.
rows.calls: One of four preview calls held

rows.head: Connelly scores with less than two minutes left to lift the Golden Knights
rows.story: Anton Johansson struck first for the Red Wings early in the third, but Braeden Bowman made it 1-1 for Vegas a little over two minutes later. Trevor Connelly put the Golden Knights ahead for good with less than two minutes left.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

rows.head: Mikheyev scores against his old team
rows.story: Victor Hedman got the scoring started for the Lightning on the power play early in the first. Ilya Mikheyev stretched the lead to 2-0 late in the period, in his first game against Chicago since leaving. Dillon Boucher and Jeffrey Viel fought early in the second.
rows.calls: Two of three preview calls held

rows.head: Nichushkin seals it in the shootout
rows.story: Mikko Rantanen got the scoring started for the Stars early in the third, but Zach Werenski tied it 1-1 for Columbus with a little over three minutes left. Valeri Nichushkin and Kent Johnson scored in the shootout for the Blue Jackets.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

chips: First goal for a new club
rows.note: First goal for a new club
rows.head: The Jets roll past the Canucks
rows.story: Viggo Björck picked up his first NHL point. The first period was a wild one. Alex Iafallo and Cole Koepke scored just 14 seconds apart early in the period to put the Jets up 2-0.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

rows.head: The Bruins run away from the Penguins
rows.story: The first period was a wild one. Justin Brazeau opened the scoring for the Penguins midway through the period. Pavel Zacha, Mark Kastelic and Elias Lindholm scored three goals in just under seven minutes later in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 3-1 lead.

rows.head: Luneau sparks a Ducks comeback
rows.story: It was a busy first period. William Strömgren struck first for the Flames early in the period, but Jeff Malott tied it 1-1 for Anaheim 27 seconds later. Joel Hanley and Joel Farabee scored two and a half minutes apart late in the period to put the Flames up 3-1, and that was all they would get.
rows.calls: One of four preview calls held

rows.head: Power has three assists as the Sabres take down the Blue Jackets
rows.story: Jack Quinn got the scoring started for the Sabres early in the first, but Kent Johnson made it 1-1 for Columbus late in the period. Josh Norris put the Sabres back ahead 2-1 just over two minutes later. Rasmus Dahlin extended the lead to 3-1 early in the second, and Norris scored again midway through the period to make it 4-1.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Four points for Kaprizov as the Wild beat the Sharks
rows.story: Kirill Kaprizov opened the scoring for the Wild on the power play early in the first. Macklin Celebrini tied it up for San Jose midway through the second, but that was the last goal the Sharks would get. Maxim Shabanov put the Wild back ahead 2-1 on the power play just over two minutes later.
rows.calls: One of four preview calls held

rows.head: Tolvanen returns to Seattle
rows.story: The Kraken (9-5-1) beat Calgary 2-1 in overtime on Wednesday, and the Rangers have won two in a row. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Kraken third in the Pacific (tied for 14th). The Rangers’ record (.559) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: Kuzmenko returns to Los Angeles
rows.story: The Kings (5-7-2) beat San Jose 7-2 on Wednesday, while the Penguins are winless in four (0-3-1). Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Penguins are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Kings seventh in the Pacific (tied for 28th).

rows.head: McDavid’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Oilers (11-3-3) lost 5-4 to Anaheim on Thursday, and the Canucks are on a four-game losing streak. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Oilers first in the Pacific (tied for third in the NHL).

rows.head: Kucherov’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Tampa Bay on Oct 8. The Wild have won three straight, and the Lightning have won two in a row. Two of the league’s best teams meet.

rows.head: The Islanders can’t afford to take penalties
rows.story: The Islanders won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-0 on Long Island on Oct 3. The Islanders (7-6-2) lost 5-3 to Carolina on Thursday, while the Devils have won three straight. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Devils second (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Isles fifth (tied for 21st).

rows.head: Round two in Nashville
rows.story: The Predators won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Nashville on Oct 17. The Preds have won three straight, while the Blues (7-7-2) lost 5-4 in overtime to New Jersey on Thursday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Blues sixth (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Predators fifth (tied for 14th).

rows.head: Open season on the Maple Leafs’ net
rows.story: The Canadiens already played in Toronto once this season and left with a 3-2 win on Sep 29. The Canadiens (10-3-3) beat Utah 5-4 in overtime on Thursday, while the Maple Leafs (8-7-2) lost 3-2 to Utah on Tuesday. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Canadiens second (sixth in the NHL) and the Maple Leafs seventh (19th).

rows.head: Iron sharpens iron
rows.story: The Mammoth (10-6-1) lost 5-4 in overtime to Montréal on Thursday, while the Senators (10-6-1) beat Buffalo 2-1 on Wednesday. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Senators fourth in the Atlantic (tied for ninth). The Mammoth have played better than their record (.618) says: their chances are worth about .730, and their goaltending has held them back.

rows.head: Rantanen’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Stars won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-0 in Dallas on Oct 5. The Stars (9-5-2) lost 2-1 in a shootout to Columbus on Thursday, and the Sharks are on a four-game losing streak. Going in, the Sharks are sixth in the Pacific (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Stars third in the Central (tied for 11th).

rows.note: Red Wings PP vs. Avalanche PK
rows.head: Who blinks first?
rows.story: The Red Wings (7-7-3) lost 2-1 to Vegas on Thursday, and the Avalanche (9-6-2) lost 3-2 in overtime to Nashville the same night. Going in, the Wings are last in the Atlantic (20th in the NHL) and the Avalanche fourth in the Central (tied for 11th). The Red Wings have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .597, and their finishing has held them back.

rows.head: Special teams lean toward the Panthers
rows.story: The Panthers (9-5-2) beat Chicago 5-3 on Wednesday, while the Capitals (8-6-0) lost 6-5 to Dallas on Tuesday. Going in, the Panthers are fifth in the Atlantic (tied for 11th in the NHL) and the Capitals fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 21st). The Panthers forecheck harder than anyone (1st), hit a lot (1st) and kill penalties well (1st).

rows.head: The Blackhawks need a win
rows.story: The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Chicago on Oct 10. The Hurricanes (13-3-2) beat the Islanders 5-3 on Thursday, while the Blackhawks are winless in five (0-4-1). Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Hurricanes are first in the NHL.

rows.head: Somebody warn Sergei Bobrovsky
rows.story: The Maple Leafs (8-7-2) lost 3-2 to Utah on Tuesday, while the Devils have won three straight. Going in, the Devils are second in the Metropolitan (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Leafs seventh in the Atlantic (19th). The Devils have played better than their record (.688) says: their chances are worth about .745, and their goaltending has held them back.

rows.head: The Golden Knights’ edge in preventing dangerous shots
rows.story: The Sabres (8-5-3) beat Columbus 5-2 on Friday, and the Golden Knights have won two in a row. Going in, the Knights are second in the Pacific (fifth in the NHL) and the Sabres sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 14th). The Golden Knights’ record (.667) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: The Panthers played last night
rows.story: The Bruins have won three straight, the last a 6-2 rout of Pittsburgh. The Panthers (9-5-2) beat Chicago 5-3 on Wednesday. The Panthers played last night, and the Bruins are rested.

rows.head: The schedule did the Lightning no favors
rows.story: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-4 in Tampa Bay on Oct 29. Both teams have won two in a row. The Lightning played last night, and the Jets are rested.

rows.head: The Flames are going to test Dan Vladař early and often
rows.story: The Flyers (4-10-4) lost 3-2 to the Rangers on Thursday, and the Flames (7-9-1) lost 5-3 to Anaheim on Friday. Going in, the Flyers are last in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Flames fifth in the Pacific (tied for 24th). The Flyers haven’t played well, but their record (.333) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .387, and their finishing has held them back.

rows.head: The Ducks are rolling
rows.story: The Ducks have won four straight, while the Penguins are winless in four (0-3-1). The Penguins played last night, and the Ducks are rested. Going in, the Pens are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Ducks fourth in the Pacific (tied for 14th).

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
rows.story: The Oilers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in New York on Nov 1. The Oilers (11-3-3) lost 5-4 to Anaheim on Thursday, while the Rangers have won two in a row. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Oilers first in the Pacific (tied for third).

rows.head: Somebody has to win
rows.story: The Canucks are on a four-game losing streak, and the Flyers (4-10-4) lost 3-2 to the Rangers on Thursday. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. The Flyers played last night, and the Canucks are rested.

rows.head: The Sharks need a win
rows.story: The Sharks are on a four-game losing streak, and the Islanders (7-6-2) lost 5-3 to Carolina on Thursday. Going in, the Islanders are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Sharks sixth in the Pacific (tied for 24th). The Islanders get their defensemen shooting (1st) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd).

standout.head: Zayne Parekh blocked 6 shots
standout.sub: Only 17 other games this season have matched it. Blocked shots as the home scorer recorded them.
